subject: chemistry
title: Relative formula mass and percentage by mass
key_idea: The relative formula mass (Mr) of a compound is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in its formula. The percentage by mass of an element is its share of the Mr, written as a percentage.

blocks.text: Every atom has a relative atomic mass (Ar). Adding the Ar values of all the atoms in a formula gives the relative formula mass.

items.meaning: The average mass of an atom of an element compared with a carbon-12 atom, which is 12. It is given in the question or on the periodic table.
The sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in the numbers shown in the formula.
The relative formula mass of a molecule. It is worked out in the same way.

items.text: A small number applies to the atom or bracket in front of it. In Ca(OH)₂ there is 1 Ca, 2 O and 2 H.
Multiply each Ar by the number of atoms of that element.
Add the results. Mr has no units.

blocks.label: Worked example: Mr of carbonic acid, H₂CO₃
where: Ar of H = 1, with 2 hydrogen atoms.
Ar of C = 12, with 1 carbon atom.
Ar of O = 16, with 3 oxygen atoms.

items: For a bracket, multiply everything inside it. In Mg(NO₃)₂ there are 2 N and 6 O.
In a balanced equation, the Mr of the reactants, in the quantities shown, adds up to the Mr of the products.
Use the Ar values given in the question, or on the periodic table.

diagram.alt: Calculate the relative formula mass of an alkane.
diagram.question: An alkane has the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Calculate the relative formula mass of the alkane with {c} carbon atoms in each molecule. (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1)

items: Mr is the sum of the Ar values of all the atoms in the formula.
Multiply by the number of atoms, including those inside brackets.

blocks.text: The percentage by mass of an element shows how much of a compound's mass is that element.

blocks.label: Percentage by mass of an element in a compound
blocks.formula: percentage by mass = (Ar × number of atoms of the element ÷ Mr of the compound) × 100
where: Ar is the relative atomic mass of the element.
Mr is the relative formula mass of the whole compound.

items.text: Ar × number of atoms. For oxygen in Li₂SO₄: 4 × 16 = 64.
Use the Mr given, or work it out. For Li₂SO₄ it is 110.

items: The percentages of all the elements in a compound add up to 100 %.
If a percentage is given, find the mass of an element as a share of a sample. Mass of element = percentage ÷ 100 × mass of sample.
The mass of the other element is the total mass minus the mass you found.

diagram.alt: Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in a compound.
diagram.question: A compound has a relative formula mass of {mr}. Each formula unit contains {n} oxygen atoms. Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in the compound. (Relative atomic mass: O = 16)

items: Percentage by mass = (Ar × number of atoms ÷ Mr) × 100.
Use the number of atoms of the element in the formula.
Give the answer to the number of significant figures asked for.

checks.q: Calculate the relative formula mass of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. (Ar: Ca = 40, O = 16, H = 1)
Calculate the percentage by mass of magnesium in magnesium oxide, MgO. (Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16)
A compound is 34.4 % iron by mass. Calculate the mass of iron in 125 g of the compound.

exam_phrases: allow correct use of an incorrectly determined mass of oxygen
allow an answer correctly rounded to 3 significant figures from an incorrect calculation

mistakes.right: Use the number of atoms. Three iron atoms give 3 × 56 = 168, so 168 ÷ 232 × 100 = 72.4 %.
There are four oxygen atoms. The mass of oxygen is 4 × 16 = 64, so 64 ÷ 110 × 100 = 58 %.

mistakes.wrong: 58.18 % given when the question asks for 2 significant figures.
mistakes.right: The last mark is for rounding as asked: 58 %. Always check the number of significant figures.

worked_example.question:
The most common oxides of iron are Fe₂O₃ and Fe₃O₄.

Calculate the percentage (%) by mass of iron in Fe₃O₄.

Relative atomic masses (Ar): O = 16, Fe = 56

Percentage by mass of iron = _____ %
worked_example.tip: A correctly calculated value from an incorrect Mr still earns credit if the working uses the given Ar values.

exam_phrases: if Mr incorrect, must show working to allow ECF

mistakes.right: There are two sodium atoms. Use 46 ÷ 106 × 100 = 43.4 %. The answer 21.7 earns 2 marks, not 3.
34.4 % is the iron. Mass of iron = 43 g. Then mass of chlorine = 125 − 43 = 82 g.

mistakes.wrong: Writing only the final answer after a long Mr calculation, with a wrong Mr.
mistakes.right: Show the working. If the Mr is wrong, marks can only follow through when the working is shown.

worked_example.question:
Sodium carbonate has the formula Na₂CO₃.

Calculate the percentage by mass of sodium in sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃.

percentage by mass of element = (total relative atomic mass of element ÷ relative formula mass of compound) × 100

(relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)
worked_example.tip: 43.4 with or without working scores 3. Show the working in case the answer is wrong.

exam_phrases: correct use of number of atoms

mistakes.right: The bracket applies to O and H. Use correct number of atoms: (1 × 40.1) + [(16.0 + 1.0) × 2] = 74.1.

mistakes.wrong: Percentage of iron in rust = 55.8 ÷ 213.6 × 100, using one iron atom.
mistakes.right: The mass of iron is 2 × 55.8, not 55.8. Use (2 × 55.8) ÷ 213.6 × 100 = 52.25 %, to 2 decimal places.
Mr has no units. Units given are ignored, but do not add them.

worked_example.question:
Calculate the relative formula mass of a (C₂H₅)₂O molecule.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0
worked_example.tip: The bracket is multiplied by 2, so there are 4 C and 10 H. The answer 74 with no working scores 3 marks.
